candidates.title: Field and temperature scaling of the critical current density in commercial REBCO coated conductors (Senatore et al. 2015)
candidates.notes: Open-access arxiv paper. Covers Jc(T,B,θ) for six commercial REBCO manufacturers at T = 4.2–77 K and B up to 19 T with a 3-parameter scaling law. Scaling relation allows extrapolation to 20–40 T at 20 K to assess feasibility of Renaissance Fusion's peak coil field range. Does not go above 19 T experimentally but provides the validated extrapolation framework.

candidates.title: JNM blanket paper — partially addresses G-9
candidates.notes: Extracted as part of G-4. The JNM paper mentions liquid metal operating temperature of 700–900 °C, which is the first wall / blanket outlet temperature range feeding the power conversion system. This partially constrains the sCO₂ turbine inlet temperature and thus the 49–51% efficiency claim. However, the ECM paper (Fama et al. 2023, doi:10.1016/j.enconman.2022.116572) likely provides the specific temperature more precisely as the heat source inlet to the sCO₂ cycle. That paper was not searched for open-access versions in this iteration.

summary.notes: Two `not-yet-sourced` gaps fully addressed with source extractions (G-4, G-11). G-4 (TBR, blocking): full JNM blanket paper extracted from EPFL open-access repository — confirms TBR ∼ 1.60 and provides 700–900 °C liquid metal temperature (partial G-9 coverage). G-11 (REBCO Jc): Senatore et al. 2015 Jc scaling law extracted from arxiv — provides validated 3-parameter scaling to extrapolate REBCO performance to 20–40 T at 20 K. G-7 (plasma parameters/ISS04): two promising open-access sources identified (IAEA ISS04 PDF, MDPI optimization paper) but both failed extraction; ISS04 formula documented in search results for analyst use. G-9 (Li-LiH outlet temperature): partially covered by JNM paper (700–900 °C range); primary source (Fama et al. ECM 2023) not searched for open-access version — recommended for next iteration. G-12 and G-13 remain unaddressed — no public sources found for HTS cylinder count or cryogenic system sizing specific to Renaissance Fusion design.
